question: Is there any correlation between ratings and violations among the restaurants?
output_text:
## Finding
There is a **weak inverse relationship** between Google ratings and recorded inspection violations among the **139 restaurants with matched SLCHD inspection histories**: higher-rated restaurants tend to have somewhat fewer cumulative violations, but ratings are not a reliable proxy for inspection performance.

- Rating vs. **total violations**: Pearson correlation **r = −0.246**.
- Rating vs. **critical violations**: **r = −0.101**, which is very weak.
- Rating vs. **most-recent inspection score**: **r = −0.157**. (Higher inspection scores indicate more cited issues in this dataset.)

### By rating band
| Google rating band | Restaurants | Avg. total violations | Avg. critical violations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Below 4.0 | 36 | 45.0 | 11.5 |
| 4.0–4.4 | 52 | 39.1 | 10.6 |
| 4.5–4.6 | 33 | 37.9 | 11.3 |
| 4.7+ | 18 | 23.6 | 8.7 |

The highest-rated group (4.7+) averaged **23.6 total** and **8.7 critical** violations, versus **45.0 total** and **11.5 critical** among restaurants rated below 4.0. But the middle rating bands overlap substantially, especially for critical violations, so a strong “better reviews = safer restaurant” conclusion is not supported.

### Important limitation
This analysis is limited to the **139 matched establishments**. Per the dataset coverage, **98.4% of establishments have no matched SLCHD inspection history**, so their absence does **not** mean they were clean or had no violations. Also, violation totals are cumulative across available inspection history, so restaurants with more inspections or longer observed histories can accumulate more citations.

### Visualization
The scatterplot shows the restaurant-level spread behind these correlations: ratings alone do not cleanly separate low- and high-violation establishments.

args.query: WITH matched AS (SELECT e.gmap_id, e.avg_rating, e.num_of_reviews, e.slchd_establishment_key, COUNT(v.violation_id) AS total_violations, COUNT(v.violation_id) FILTER (WHERE vc.critical) AS critical_violations, MAX(i.inspection_score) FILTER (WHERE i.inspection_date = (SELECT MAX(i2.inspection_date) FROM inspections i2 WHERE i2.slchd_establishment_key=e.slchd_establishment_key)) AS latest_score FROM establishments e JOIN inspections i ON i.slchd_establishment_key=e.slchd_establishment_key LEFT JOIN violations v ON v.inspection_id=i.inspection_id LEFT JOIN violation_codes vc ON vc.violation_code_id=v.violation_code_id WHERE e.avg_rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.gmap_id,e.avg_rating,e.num_of_reviews,e.slchd_establishment_key) SELECT COUNT(*) AS matched_restaurants, corr(avg_rating, total_violations) AS pearson_rating_total_violations, corr(avg_rating, critical_violations) AS pearson_rating_critical_violations, corr(avg_rating, latest_score) AS pearson_rating_latest_score, corr(num_of_reviews, total_violations) AS pearson_reviews_total_violations FROM matched;

WITH matched AS (SELECT e.gmap_id, avg_rating, COUNT(v.violation_id) AS total_violations, COUNT(v.violation_id) FILTER (WHERE vc.critical) AS critical_violations FROM establishments e JOIN inspections i ON i.slchd_establishment_key=e.slchd_establishment_key LEFT JOIN violations v ON v.inspection_id=i.inspection_id LEFT JOIN violation_codes vc ON vc.violation_code_id=v.violation_code_id WHERE avg_rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.gmap_id,avg_rating) SELECT CASE WHEN avg_rating < 4.0 THEN 'Below 4.0' WHEN avg_rating < 4.5 THEN '4.0–4.4' WHEN avg_rating < 4.7 THEN '4.5–4.6' ELSE '4.7+' END AS rating_band, COUNT(*) AS restaurants, ROUND(AVG(total_violations),1) AS avg_total_violations, ROUND(AVG(critical_violations),1) AS avg_critical_violations FROM matched GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE rating_band WHEN 'Below 4.0' THEN 1 WHEN '4.0–4.4' THEN 2 WHEN '4.5–4.6' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END;

WITH matched AS (SELECT e.gmap_id, e.name, e.avg_rating, COUNT(v.violation_id) AS total_violations, COUNT(v.violation_id) FILTER (WHERE vc.critical) AS critical_violations FROM establishments e JOIN inspections i ON i.slchd_establishment_key=e.slchd_establishment_key LEFT JOIN violations v ON v.inspection_id=i.inspection_id LEFT JOIN violation_codes vc ON vc.violation_code_id=v.violation_code_id WHERE e.avg_rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.gmap_id,e.name,e.avg_rating) SELECT avg_rating, total_violations, critical_violations, name FROM matched ORDER BY avg_rating;

- Rating vs. **most-recent inspection score**: **r = −0.157**. (Higher inspection scores indicate more cited issues in this dataset.)

### By rating band
| Google rating band | Restaurants | Avg. total violations | Avg. critical violations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Below 4.0 | 36 | 45.0 | 11.5 |
| 4.0–4.4 | 52 | 39.1 | 10.6 |
| 4.5–4.6 | 33 | 37.9 | 11.3 |
| 4.7+ | 18 | 23.6 | 8.7 |

The highest-rated group (4.7+) averaged **23.6 total** and **8.7 critical** violations, versus **45.0 total** and **11.5 critical** among restaurants rated below 4.0. But the middle rating bands overlap substantially, especially for critical violations, so a strong “better reviews = safer restaurant” conclusion is not supported.

### Important limitation
This analysis is limited to the **139 matched establishments**. Per the dataset coverage, **98.4% of establishments have no matched SLCHD inspection history**, so their absence does **not** mean they were clean or had no violations. Also, violation totals are cumulative across available inspection history, so restaurants with more inspections or longer observed histories can accumulate more citations.
